A thoughtful start.

The current beta needs a Watch normally paired with an iPhone. Apple Family Setup is not supported in this beta.

Before buying hardware: confirm release compatibility with us. The website preview needs no Watch or account.

What is present in the native app?

Current source includes questions, discoveries, stories, early math, topic preferences, and saved activity reports. The homepage recreates the current Curiosity and Parent Dock designs. These are source-grounded website renderings, not a connected native session or a promise of final release UI.

Features remain in testing. Source implementation does not establish that every native behavior, safeguard, sync state, or data-handling process has been verified. Reports do not include every offline experience.

What can I try on this website?

Three prepared discoveries, a complete narrated story, a short garden math activity, and illustrative parent controls. Moon preferences, listening pace, and a completed-sample list work in this browser only. The iPhone tour separately shows the current native design with fictional example data.

No live AI, microphone, real child account, or physical device connection is involved.

What needs to happen before release?

Compatibility, onboarding, and parent controls need release validation. App-specific data practices, providers, retention, consent, and account deletion also need verified disclosures.

No public App Store availability, launch date, subscription pricing, or broader age support is announced here. The absence of ads does not establish regulatory compliance.

Is it a screen-free or school-time device?

TrustinJr is audio-first. It also uses pictures, readable text, and touch interactions, so we do not call it screen-free.

The app is not positioned as a school-time device. Follow your school’s device policies.
